description: GHSA advisories that have been explicitly risk-accepted at Level 2 by the CTO (SEC-04/TAH-24; TAH-34). Each entry records the issue the decision was made on in its rationale and acceptedBy. .github/scripts/check-npm-audit-allowlist.mjs fails the `npm audit` CI job on any advisory that is not listed here, or whose reviewBy date has passed. Do not add an entry without a recorded Level 2 risk-acceptance decision.

accepted.title: PostCSS has XSS via Unescaped </style> in its CSS Stringify Output
accepted.rationale: SEC-04: unreachable in this application — exploitation requires attacker-controlled CSS input or a crafted sourceMappingURL comment. This app only ever compiles first-party CSS through the Next.js build; it never parses user-supplied stylesheets.

accepted.title: PostCSS: Arbitrary file read and information disclosure via attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL in CSS comments
accepted.rationale: SEC-04: unreachable — same first-party-CSS-only reasoning as GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93; no user-supplied CSS or source maps are ever processed.

accepted.title: PostCSS: incomplete fix of GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q — attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL reads arbitrary .map files when `from` is unset
accepted.rationale: SEC-04: unreachable — the incomplete-fix follow-up to GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q; same first-party-CSS-only reasoning applies.

accepted.title: PostCSS: Path Traversal in Previous Source Map Auto-Loading (sourceMappingURL) leads to Arbitrary .map File Disclosure
accepted.rationale: SEC-04: unreachable — same first-party-CSS-only reasoning; no attacker-controlled source maps are ever auto-loaded.

accepted.title: DeepmergeTS has stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs
accepted.rationale: SEC-04: reached only through @prisma/config in the Prisma CLI/migration tooling path, not the application request path — never invoked on untrusted runtime input.

accepted.title: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns
accepted.rationale: TAH-34: unreachable in this application — pulled in solely via eslint-config-next (devDependency) -> @next/eslint-plugin-next -> fast-glob -> micromatch -> braces, and marked dev-only in package-lock.json, so it is never part of the Next.js build output or the server runtime. It only runs during `npm run lint`, expanding repo-authored glob patterns; the deeply nested pattern that triggers the stack exhaustion would have to be committed to our own lint config by us. No upstream fix exists: braces@3.0.3 is the latest published version and the advisory range is <=3.0.3, and micromatch@4.0.8 (latest) still depends on braces ^3.0.3, so an `overrides` pin has nothing to pin to. The npm-suggested downgrade to eslint-config-next@14.2.35 was tested and is not a net improvement — it trades this advisory for a different unreachable high (GHSA-5j98-mcp5-4vw2, glob CLI command injection) at the cost of a semver-major lint-config downgrade. Re-evaluate when braces publishes a patched release.
